IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p3/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p3/r10.speaker: آخر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p3/r10.claim: An unnamed interpreter claims al-wayl is a valley in Hell; Ibn Qutayba rejects this as unsound interpretation.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p3/r10.anchor: وقال الآخر في قوله: {ويل للمطففين} (4) إن الويل: واد في جهنم.

BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r1.claim: Wayl means severe evil, ruin, or painful punishment; Ibn Kaysan calls it the utterance of a distressed person in affliction, implying that the addressee deserves calamity, while another derivation links it to sorrow.
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r1.anchor: شدة الشر أو الهلاك أو العذاب الأليم ، وقال ابن كيسان

BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r2.claim: Wayl can begin a sentence despite being indefinite because it functions as a curse or prayer for harm, as discussed earlier in al-Mursalat.
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r2.anchor: وهو مبتدأ وإن كان نكرة لوقوعه في موقع الدعاء

BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r3.claim: Mutaffifin are those who deprive people of their rights in measuring and weighing; tatfif is secretly cheating by giving a buyer less than the full due, often in a slight amount that escapes notice.
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r3.anchor: فإن التطفيف البخس في الكيل والوزن والنقص والخيانة فيهما بأن لا يعطي المشتري حقه تاما كاملا

BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r4.claim: Al-Raghib defines short-measuring as reducing the buyer’s share when fulfilling a measure; Sa‘di al-Mufti says the intensive pattern suits their habitual cheating, though it could be causative.
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r4.anchor: يقال طفف الكيل قلل نصيب المكيل له في إيفائه واستيفائه

BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r5.claim: A report says the Prophet arrived in Medina when its people were among the worst measurers, recited the newly revealed surah, and five public wrongs brought five calamities; after they complied, they became the fairest measurers.
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r5.anchor: روى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قدم المدينة وكان أهلها من أبخس الناس كيلا

BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r6.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r6.claim: Ali saw a man weighing saffron and adding extra; he told him first to establish the proper measure, then to give extra as he wished, distinguishing obligation from charity.
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r6.anchor: إنه مر برجل يزن الزعفران وقد أرجح فقال أقم الوزن بالقسط

BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas warns non-Arabs that measure and scale were the two practices by which earlier peoples perished, singling them out because they used both methods together.
BURSEVI:v10p281#2/r7.anchor: إنكم معشر الأعاجم وليتم أمرين بهما هلك من كان قبلكم

QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.claim: Beyond literal cheating in measures, the verses concern cheating on the true scale of justice, where character and deeds are measured.
QASHANI:83:1-5/r1.anchor: يمكن أن يحمل بعد الظاهر على التطفيف في الميزان الحقيقي الذي هو العدل، والموزونات به هي الأخلاق والأعمال

QUSHAYRI:v3p401/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p401/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p401/r1.claim: God’s name is marked by majesty and beauty; His existence has no beginning, kindness is what people expect, and whatever He decrees is His rightful command.
QUSHAYRI:v3p401/r1.anchor: الوجود له غير مستفتح ، والموجود منه غير مستقبح ، المعهود منه لطفه

QUSHAYRI:v3p401/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p401/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p401/r2.claim: Woe is an expression used when calamity occurs; a cheater is one who gives short measure or weight.
QUSHAYRI:v3p401/r2.anchor: الويل كلمة تذكر عند وقوع البلاء ، فيقال : ويل لك

SULAMI:v2p380/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p380/r1.speaker: أبو صالح حمدون
SULAMI:v2p380/r1.claim: When holding a scale, remember the scale of justice that will weigh you and fear the threatened woe.
SULAMI:v2p380/r1.anchor: قال أبو صالح حمدون : إذا أخذت الميزان بيدك فاذكر ميزان القسط عليك

SULAMI:v2p380/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p380/r2.speaker: أبو صالح حمدون
SULAMI:v2p380/r2.claim: One who sees a brother's faults while blind to his own commits the same kind of short measure.
SULAMI:v2p380/r2.anchor: وقال أيضا : ويل لمن يبصر عيوب أخيه ، ويعمى عن عيوبه فإن ذلك التطفيف

SULAMI:v2p380/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p380/r3.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v2p380/r3.claim: Defrauders take all their rights but fail to fulfill others' rights, and condemn faults in others that they themselves commit even worse.
SULAMI:v2p380/r3.anchor: سئل أبو حفص عن قوله : ﴿ ويل للمطففين ﴾ قال : الذي يستوفى حقه من الخلق

SULAMI:v2p380/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p380/r4.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p380/r4.claim: The verse also condemns those who perform worship for people to see but neglect it in private.
SULAMI:v2p380/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان : حقيقة هذه الآية والله أعلم عندي هو : من يحسن العبادة على رؤية الناس

TUSTARI:83:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:83:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:83:1/r1.claim: Defrauders are hypocrites and their imitators who short-measure in prayer; Sulayman compares prayer to a measure that is repaid in kind.
TUSTARI:83:1/r1.anchor: قال: هم المنافقون ومن تخلق بأخلاقهم، يطففون في صلاتهم، كما قال سليمان رضي الله عنه: الصلاة مكيال

TUSTARI:83:1/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:83:1/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:83:1/r2.claim: They condemn others' faults while committing the same or worse; the verse recalls the rebuke against telling others to do good while forgetting oneself.
TUSTARI:83:1/r2.anchor: وتغمزونهم على ما عثروا عليه من عيوب الناس، وترتكبون مثلها وأفظع منها.

TUSTARI:83:1/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:83:1/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:83:1/r3.claim: Only the ignorant inspect people's slips, and revealing a secret one has learned is accursed.
TUSTARI:83:1/r3.anchor: ولا يطلع على عثرات الخلق إلا مخطئ جاهل، ولا يهتك سر ما اطلع عليه إلا ملعون.

TUSTARI:83:1/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:83:1/r4.speaker: الله
TUSTARI:83:1/r4.claim: In a revelation to David, God says people sin in private and repent publicly, though He does not want their servant's sin exposed to others.
TUSTARI:83:1/r4.anchor: الله تعالى أوحى إلى داود عليه السلام: أشكو إليك عبادي يا داود. فقال: ولم يا رب؟ قال: لأنهم يذنبون في السر ويتوبون في العلانية

FARRA:v3p245#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p245#2/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p245#2/r1.claim: The warning was revealed on the Prophet's arrival in Medina: buyers took extra measure or weight, sellers shorted them; they stopped and became exceptionally accurate.
FARRA:v3p245#2/r1.anchor: نزلت أول قدوم النبي صلى الله عليه إلى المدينة

FARRA:v3p245#2/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p245#2/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p245#2/r2.claim: Some say ويل is a valley in Hell; al-Farrāʾ distinguishes that report from the familiar word ويل.

MAJAZ:v2p289/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p289/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p289/r1.claim: A mutaffif is someone who fails to give people their full measure.
MAJAZ:v2p289/r1.anchor: «ويل للمطففين» (1) المطفف الذي لا يوفى على الناس

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3409/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3409/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3409/r1.claim: Ibn Umar answers Hilal ibn Talq's question about whether Meccans or Medinans best fulfill measures by saying they deserve the warning against defrauders in this verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3409/r1.anchor: مع ابن عمر فقلت : من احسن الناس هيئة وافاه كيلا ؟ اهل مكة أو المدينة ؟ قال : حق لهم ، اما سمعت الله يقول : ويل للمطففين

NAHHAS:v5p173/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p173/r1.claim: ويل is nominative as a subject and للمطففين its predicate, with ويل meaning reproof.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r1.anchor: رفعت ويلا بالابتداء للمطففين خبره أي تأنيب

NAHHAS:v5p173/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p173/r2.claim: Accusative is possible outside the Quran because ويل is a verbal noun, but nominative is preferred since no verb is derived from it except rare forms.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r2.anchor: ويجوز النصب في غير القرآن لأن ويلا بمعنى المصدر وكان الاختيار الرفع لأنه لا ينطق منه بفعل

NAHHAS:v5p173/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r3.speaker: محمد بن الوليد
NAHHAS:v5p173/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Walid cites the rare forms وال, واح, and واس as evidence that verbs from ويل are exceptional.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r3.anchor: أنشده محمد بن الوليد وهو ( فما وال ولا واح

NAHHAS:v5p173/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r4.speaker: النحويون
NAHHAS:v5p173/r4.claim: If ويل is derived from a verb, grammarians prefer its accusative, as in بؤسا له.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r4.anchor: فإن كان مشتقا من فعل فالاختيار النصب عند النحويين نحو بؤسا له

NAHHAS:v5p173/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p173/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p173/r5.claim: If the predicate is omitted in an initial construction, one can instead say ويله or ويحه.
NAHHAS:v5p173/r5.anchor: وإن لم يأت بالخبر في الأول نصبت فقلت ويله وويحه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r1.claim: Wayl denotes destruction, grief, and enduring misery; a report from Ibn Masʿud and others says it is a valley in Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r1.anchor: ويل معناه: الثبور والحزن والشقاء الأدوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r2.claim: ويل is nominative as a subject meaning the threat is established for them; expressions of wishing or awaiting are instead accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r2.anchor: على الابتداء، ورفع على معنى ثبت لهم واستقر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r3.claim: A mutaffif shortchanges others; the root refers to a tiny amount because the shortfall is slight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r3.anchor: و «المطفف» : الذي ينقص الناس حقوقهم، والتطفيف:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r4.speaker: سلمان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r4.claim: Salman likens prayer to a measure: whoever completes it is rewarded fully, while the one who shortchanges it faces the warning about defrauders.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r4.anchor: وقال سلمان: الصلاة مكيال، فمن أوفى وفي له،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r5.claim: Some scholars extend tatfif to every word and deed; ʿUmar used it to say he fell short in work and reward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: يدخل التطفيف في كل قول وعمل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r6.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r6.claim: Malik says every matter can be fulfilled or shortchanged; some define tatfif as exceeding the due amount in either direction, a view Ibn ʿAṭiyya judges sound with context determining the intent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p449#2/r6.anchor: وكذا قال مالك رحمه الله: يقال لكل شيء وفاء وتطفيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that when the Prophet arrived in Medina, its people were the worst at measuring; after this verse was revealed, they measured properly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says the Prophet arrived in Medina when Abū Juhayna used two measures, one for measuring out and one for measuring in, and the verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r2.anchor: وقال السدي قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة وبها رجل يقال له أبو جهينة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines a defrauder as one who fails to give full measure; a vessel that is not full is called “ṭafān.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r3.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة المطفف الذي لا يوفي الكيل يقال إناء طفان إذا لم يكن مملوءا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says they are called defrauders because they take only a tiny amount by cheating in measure or weight; the word comes from the edge of a thing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p51/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج إنما قيل مطفف لأنه لا يكاد يسرق في الميزان والمكيال إلا الشيء الطفيف

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r1.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the chapter was revealed in Medina.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r1.anchor: واختلفوا فذكر الحسن، والضحاك أنها نزلت بالمدينة

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r2.claim: Other reports place its revelation between Mecca and Medina, in Mecca, or upon the Prophet's first arrival in Medina, respectively attributed to a group, Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Farrāʾ.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r2.anchor: وذكر جماعة أنها نزلت بين مكة والمدينة.

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r3.claim: A report promises the sealed nectar to anyone who recites Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn on the Day of Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r3.anchor: من قرأ سورة (المطففين) سقاه الله من الرحيق المختوم يوم القيامة

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r4.claim: The surah develops the preceding al-Infiṭār ending, which mentioned Resurrection and the fates of the righteous and wicked, by detailing people's conditions at Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r4.anchor: ولما ختم سورة (انفطرت) بذكر القيامة، وما أعد للأبرار والفجار

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.claim: Ṭafīf means tiny or insignificant; a mutaffif reduces another person's proper measure or weight, whether by a small shortfall or a subtle theft.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r7.anchor: الطفيف: الشيء التفه القليل، والمطفف: المقلل حق صاحبه بنقصانه

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.claim: One explanation names the act for the tiny amount missing from the rightful measure.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r8.anchor: وقيل: لأن ما ينقص منه طفيف قليل

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.claim: Another view calls the act a secret theft of a small amount.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r9.anchor: وقيل: التطفيف: أن يسرق الشيء اليسير في خفية

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.claim: Related usage describes an underfilled vessel and says all descendants of Adam are close to a full measure.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r10.anchor: وإناء طفان إذا لم يكن ملآن، ومنه: بنو آدم كلهم طف الصاع

JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.claim: No one has superiority over another except through piety.
JISHUMI:v10p7317/r11.anchor: فليس لأحد على أحد فضل إلا بالتقوى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r1.claim: Tatfif is cheating in measure or weight by shorting someone a slight, trifling amount.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r1.anchor: التطفيف : البخس في الكيل والوزن : لأن ما يبخس شيء طفيف حقير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r2.claim: A report says the people of Medina were the worst measurers when the Prophet arrived; the warning came down and they improved their measuring.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قدم المدينة وكانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا ، فنزلت فأحسنوا الكيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r3.claim: Another account says a Medinan called Abu Juhaynah had two measures, using one when selling and another when buying.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r3.anchor: وقيل : قدمها وبها رجل يعرف بأبي جهينة ومعه صاعان : بكيل بأحدهما ويكتال بالآخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r4.claim: A further report says Medinan merchants cheated in trade through munabadha, mulamasa, and mukhatara; the surah came down and the Prophet recited it to them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r4.anchor: كان أهل المدينة تجارا يطففون ، وكانت بياعاتهم المنابذة والملامسة والمخاطرة ، فنزلت فخرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقرأها عليهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r5.claim: A report says five social violations bring five calamities: breaking covenants brings enemy domination; judging without revelation spreads poverty; public indecency spreads death; cheating measures withholds crops and brings drought; withholding zakat blocks rain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r5.anchor: ما نقض قوم العهد إلا سلط الله عليهم عدوهم ، وما حكموا بغير ما أنزل الله إلا فشا فيهم الفقر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r6.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r6.claim: Ali told a man who was weighing saffron with an excess to establish the fair weight first, then add whatever he wished, habituating fairness and distinguishing duty from extra giving.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r6.anchor: مر برجل يزن الزعفران وقد أرجح فقال له : أقم الوزن بالقسط ، ثم أرجح بعد ذلك ما شئت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas warns Persians that they were entrusted with measures and scales, by which earlier peoples perished; he singles them out because they use both, unlike Mecca's weighing and Medina's measuring.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r7.anchor: إنكم معشر الأعاجم وليتم أمرين : بهما هلك من كان قبلكم : المكيال والميزان ؛ وخص الأعاجم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r8.claim: Ibn Umar warned sellers to fear God and fulfill measures, saying cheats will be halted before the Majestic Lord until sweat reaches their mouths.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r8.anchor: اتق الله وأوف الكيل ، فإن المطففين يوقفون يوم القيامة لعظمة الرحمن حتى إن العرق ليلجمهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r9.speaker: عكرمة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r9.claim: Ikrima testified that every measurer or weigher is in Hell; when told his own son did that work, he repeated the testimony about his son.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r9.anchor: أشهد أن كل كيال ووزان في النار . فقيل له : إن ابنك كيال أو وزان ؛ فقال : أشهد أنه في النار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r10.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r10.claim: Ubayy says not to seek one's needs from people who earn their living at the tops of measures and tongues of scales.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p719/r10.anchor: لا تلتمس الحوائج ممن رزقه في رؤوس المكاييل وألسن الموازين

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r1.claim: He says Medina's merchants were among the worst measurers until the warning was revealed, after which they improved.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r1.anchor: عباس : كان أهل المدينة من أخبث الناس كيلا , إلى أن أنزل الله تعالى : { ويل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r2.claim: He says they became among the most accurate in measure thereafter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r2.anchor: فأحسنوا الكيل , قال الفراء : فهم من أوفى الناس كيلا إلى يومهم هذا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r3.speaker: بعض المتعمقة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r3.claim: A mystical interpretation takes the warning as outwardly displaying complete worship before people while inwardly withholding it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r3.anchor: المتعمقة فحمله على استيفاء العبادة بين الناس جهرا , وفي النقصان سرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r4.claim: A Prophetic report identifies ويل as a valley in Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r4.anchor: أنه واد في جهنم , رواه أبو سعيد الخدري مرفوعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r5.claim: He says ويل is the pus of Hell's inhabitants.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r5.anchor: صديد أهل النار , قاله ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r6.speaker: عمر مولى عفرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r6.claim: He glosses ويل as the Fire.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r6.anchor: أنه النار , قاله عمر مولى عفرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r7.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r7.claim: Some linguists gloss ويل as destruction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r7.anchor: أنه الهلاك , قاله بعض أهل اللغة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r8.claim: Other glosses are the harshest punishment, a cry of ruin used in war and plunder, or an expression originally formed from وي لفلان.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r8.anchor: أنه أشق العذاب . السادس : أنه النداء بالخسار والهلاك , وقد تستعمله العرب في الحرب والسلب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r9.claim: A mutaffif takes a small amount from another person's due by short measure or weight; the term may derive from a little amount or the edge of a thing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r9.anchor: مأخوذ من الطفيف وهو القليل , والمطفف هو المقلل حق صاحبه بنقصانه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r10.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r10.claim: He derives mutaffif from the edge or side of a thing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p225#2/r10.anchor: الزجاج : بل مأخوذ من طف الشيء وهي جهته

MUQATIL:83:1-5/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r1.claim: He identifies wayl as a valley in Hell seventy years long, with immense nested branches and chambers containing fiery trees, worms, snakes, and scorpions.
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r1.anchor: الويل واد في جهنم بعده مسيرة سبعين سنة، فيه تسعون ألف شعب، في كل شعب سبعون ألف شق

MUQATIL:83:1-5/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r3.claim: When the Prophet arrived in Medina, he warned the traders about what they were doing.
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r3.anchor: فلما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة قال لهم: " ويل لكم مما تصنعون "

MUQATIL:83:1-5/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r4.claim: God confirmed the Prophet's warning by revealing the condemnation of those who shortmeasure.
MUQATIL:83:1-5/r4.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى التصديق على لسانه، فقال: { ويل للمطففين }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#11/r1.claim: Woe is the predicate for those who cheat, taking away people's rights in measure and weight.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p322#11/r1.anchor: ﴿ ويل ﴾ مبتدا خبره ﴿ للمطففين ﴾ للذين يبخسون حقوق الناس فى الكيل والوزن

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Medina's traders measured fraudulently when the Prophet arrived; the warning was revealed and they corrected their practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r1.anchor: روى النسائي عن ابن عباس قال: لما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r2.claim: Al-Farra says Medina's traders thereafter became among the most exact in their measures.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: فهم من أوفى الناس كيلا إلى يومهم هذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r3.claim: A second report calls this the first surah revealed upon the Prophet's arrival in Medina and says buyers took extra while sellers shortchanged customers.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا قال: هي: أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ساعة نزل المدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r4.claim: Abu Hurayrah says the verse concerned Abu Juhaynah, also named ʿAmr, who used one measure to take goods and another to sell them.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: نزلت في رجل يعرف بأبي جهينة، واسمه عمرو كان له صاعان

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r5.claim: Wayl is severe afterlife punishment; Ibn ʿAbbas also describes it as a valley in Hell flowing with pus.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إنه واد في جهنم يسيل فيه صديد أهل النار

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says a person who knowingly rents an unfair measure bears its blame.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر قال: المطفف: الرجل يستأجر المكيال وهو يعلم أنه يحيف في كيله

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r7.claim: Others extend shortchanging to measures, weights, ablution, prayer, speech, and any matter with a due amount.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: التطفيف في الكيل والوزن والوضوء والصلاة والحديث.

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r8.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives mutaffif from a tiny amount, taken at the edge; short measure fails to fill the vessel to its rim.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج: إنما قيل للفاعل من هذا مطفف لأنه لا يكاد يسرق من المكيال

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r9.speaker: ابن القاسم عن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r9.claim: Malik advises pouring goods freely until the buyer's measure is full, then releasing the hand without holding anything back.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1/r9.anchor: وروي ابن القاسم عن مالك: أنه قرأ { ويل للمطففين } فقال: لا تطفف ولا تخلب

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.claim: A Prophetic warning pairs five wrongs with consequences: broken covenants bring enemies, rejecting God's law poverty, immorality plague, short measure drought, and withholding alms the loss of rain.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r1.anchor: خمس بخمس: ما نقض قوم العهد إلا سلط الله عليهم عدوهم

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.claim: Al-Bazzar transmits the warning by gist, and Malik also relates it from Ibn ʿUmar.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r2.anchor: خرجه أبو بكر البزار بمعناه، ومالك بن أنس أيضا من حديث ابن عمر.

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.speaker: مالك بن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.claim: Malik ibn Dinar tells of a dying neighbor who used two measures and saw them grow into mountains of fire when struck together.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r3.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار: دخلت على جار لي قد نزل به الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.claim: ʿIkrimah swears every measurer or weigher is destined for Hell, even when asked whether this applies to his son.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: أشهد على كل كيال أو وزان أنه في النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.claim: Al-Asmaʿi quotes a Bedouin saying manliness cannot reside in measure rims or scale tongues; it is also related from ʿAli.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r5.anchor: قال الأصمعي: وسمعت أعرابية تقول: لا تلتمس المروءة ممن مروءته

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.speaker: عبد خير
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.claim: ʿAbd Khayr says ʿAli overturned a scale that gave excess saffron, ordering accurate weight first and voluntary excess afterward.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r6.anchor: وقال عبد خير: مر علي رضي الله عنه على رجل وهو يزن الزعفران وقد أرجح

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.claim: Nafiʿ says Ibn ʿUmar warned short-measurers will stand in sweat up to half their ears.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r7.anchor: وقال نافع: كان ابن عمر يمر بالبائع فيقول: اتق الله وأوف الكيل والوزن

QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.claim: Abu Hurayrah says Medina's deputy recited this surah at dawn; he prayed against a trader who bought with full measure but sold short.
QURTUBI-FULL:83:1-3/r8.anchor: وقرأ في الركعة الثانية «ويل للمطففين» قال أبو هريرة: فأقول في صلاتي

RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r1.claim: The surah follows the previous one: Resurrection leaves no soul in control of another and all command belongs to God, a warning to sinners that leads into the threat against defrauders.
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن اتصال أول هذه السورة بآخر السورة المتقدمة ظاهر ، لأنه تعالى بين في آخر تلك السورة

RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r2.claim: Mutaffifūn are warned against covertly short-changing a small amount in measures and weights, since larger fraud is obvious and small fraud is stopped if discovered.
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r2.anchor: والمراد الزجر عن التطفيف ، وهو البخس في المكيال والميزان بالشيء القليل على سبيل الخفية

RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r3.claim: Wayl is an expression used when calamity occurs, as in “woe to you” or “woe against you.”
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r3.anchor: الويل ، كلمة تذكر عند وقوع البلاء ، يقال : ويل لك

RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r4.claim: One etymology derives mutaffif from ṭaff, the edge or brim: a defrauder fills only up to the rim without reaching a full measure.
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r4.anchor: طف الشيء هو جانبه وحرفه ، يقال : طف الوادي والإناء

RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the name reflects the tiny amount stolen: the defrauder usually takes only something slight.
RAZI-FULL:v31p80#2/r5.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج : أنه إنما قيل للذي ينقص المكيال والميزان مطفف

RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Medinans were among the worst in measuring when the Prophet arrived; after the verse was revealed, they improved.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال : لما قدم نبي الله المدينة كانوا من أبخس الناس كيلا

RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r8.claim: Another account says Medinan merchants used risky sales such as munābadha and mulāmasa; the Prophet recited the verse and explained five communal wrongs and punishments.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r8.anchor: وقيل كان أهل المدينة تجارا يطففون وكانت بياعاتهم المنابذة والملامسة والمخاطرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r9.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r9.claim: The Prophetic report “five for five” links broken covenants to enemy domination, unjust rule to poverty, immorality to death, short measure to famine, and withheld alms to withheld rain.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81/r9.anchor: قال ما نقص قوم العهد إلا سلط الله عليهم عدوهم ، وما حكموا بغير ما أنزل الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r1.claim: Their offense combines taking extra and giving less; scholars disagree whether the threat requires fraud at theft-nisab scale or covers every amount without repentance or greater good deeds, the latter being stronger.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r1.anchor: ثم اختلف العلماء ، فقال بعضهم : هذه الآية دالة على الوعيد ، فلا تتناول إلا إذا بلغ التطفيف حد الكثير

RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r2.speaker: أصحاب الوعيد
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r2.claim: Proponents of the threat argue this verse addresses Muslims, not unbelievers: unbelief would itself explain the threat, and the resurrection warning is directed at believers.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r2.anchor: احتج أصحاب الوعيد بعموم هذه الآية ، قالوا : وهذه الآية واردة في أهل الصلاة لا في الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r3.claim: The same threat includes one who resolves to commit fraud, since the intention itself is a major sin.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r3.anchor: أن هذا الوعيد يتناول من يفعل ذلك ومن يعزم عليه إذ العزم عليه أيضا من الكبائر

RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r4.claim: Measures matter greatly because ordinary transactions depend on them; God stresses justice in weighing in 55:7–9 and the book and balance in 57:25.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r4.anchor: واعلم أن أمر المكيال والميزان عظيم ، وذلك لأن عامة الخلق يحتاجون إلى المعاملات

RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r5.claim: Qatādah urges people to fulfil measures and act fairly as they would like others to do for them.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة : ( أوف يا ابن آدم الكيل كما تحب أن يوفي لك ، واعدل كما تحب أن يعدل لك )

RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r6.speaker: الفضيل
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r6.claim: Al-Fuḍayl says cheating the balance blackens a person's face on the Day of Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r6.anchor: وعن الفضيل : بخس الميزان سواد الوجه يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r7.speaker: أعرابي
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r7.claim: A Bedouin challenged ʿAbd al-Malik: if slight defrauding earns this threat, what of taking far more and seizing Muslim property without measure or weight?
RAZI-FULL:v31p81#2/r7.anchor: وقال أعرابي لعبد الملك بن مروان : قد سمعت ما قال الله تعالى في المطففين

RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r11.speaker: القشيري
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r11.claim: Al-Qushayrī extends mutaffif to everyday dealings: hiding others' faults, overlooking one's own, demanding rights without granting them, and failing to treat a fellow Muslim as oneself; the ideal pays others' rights without demanding one's own.
RAZI-FULL:v31p83/r11.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو القاسم القشيري : لفظ المطفف يتناول التطفيف في الوزن والكيل

STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r1.claim: The sūrah may be late Makkan, early Madinan, or a combination of both.
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r1.anchor: is a late Makkan or early Madinan sūrah, or a combination of the two.

STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r2.speaker: Bg, IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r2.claim: One account places the first four verses just after the Prophet arrived in Madinah, verses 5–28 in Madinah, and the final eight among the last verses revealed in Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r2.anchor: The first four verses were reportedly revealed just after the Prophet’s arrival in Madinah

STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r4.claim: The name al-Muṭaffifīn means those who skim a little off the top, shortchanging others; the word derives from ṭafīf and ṭaff, the edge.
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r4.anchor: deriving from ṭaff, meaning “the very edge” of something

STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r5.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r5.claim: More broadly, defrauders demand that their own rights be observed while neglecting others' rights, or see others' faults but not their own.
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r5.anchor: those who ask that their own rights be observed, but are not willing to recognize the rights of others

STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah condemns shortchanging, contrasts the fates of profligates and pious people, and closes with sinners mocking the Prophet and believers.
STUDYQURAN:83:intro/r6.anchor: Beginning with a condemnation of those who shortchange others (vv. 1–6)

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r1.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r1.claim: When the Prophet first reached Madinah, its people were notorious defrauders; after revelation of these verses, they weighed honestly.
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r1.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās said, “When the Prophet first moved to Madinah, its inhabitants were the worst kind of defrauders

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r2.speaker: Abū Hurayrah
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r2.claim: The verses refer directly to a man who used separate scales for buying and selling.
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r2.anchor: According to Abū Hurayrah, these verses refer directly to a man who had two scales

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r3.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r3.claim: The Prophet linked covenant-breaking with enemies, judging apart from revelation with poverty, fornication with death, fraud with crop failure and famine, and withholding alms with withheld rain; no grading is stated.
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r3.anchor: The Prophet recited them to the citizens of Madinah and said, “Five for five.”

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r4.claim: The warning extends beyond commerce: anyone who intentionally falls short in anything ordained by God may face shame and suffering.
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r4.anchor: shame and suffering will befall anyone who intentionally falls short in any matter according to what has been ordained by God

STUDYQURAN:83:1/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r5.speaker: Ibn Masʿūd
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd compares prayer to a measure: completing it brings full reward, while reducing it recalls the warning against defrauders.
STUDYQURAN:83:1/r5.anchor: Ibn Masʿūd, a Companion of the Prophet and early Quranic commentator, said, “Prayer is a measure.

SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r1.claim: The word ويل is a nominative subject; beginning with it is licensed because it is a curse or supplication, though accusative is also possible.
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r1.anchor: مبتدأ، وسوغ الابتداء به كونه دعاء. ولو نصب لجاز

SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r2.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r2.claim: Makkī prefers nominative for ويل and similar words when not annexed, while allowing accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r2.anchor: وقال مكي: " والمختار في " ويل " وشبهه إذا كان غير مضاف الرفع. ويجوز النصب

SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r3.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r3.claim: Makkī prefers accusative when ويل is annexed or definite.
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r3.anchor: وقال مكي: " والمختار في " ويل " وشبهه إذا كان غير مضاف الرفع. ويجوز النصب، فإن كان مضافا أو معرفا كان الاختيار/ فيه النصب

SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r4.claim: للمطففين is the predicate of ويل.

SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r5.claim: A mutaffif is one who diminishes; the term specifically evokes taking a tiny, trivial amount in measuring or weighing, like the expression دون الطفيف.
SAMIN-DURR:83:1/r5.anchor: والمطفف: المنقص. وحقيقته: الأخذ في كيل، أو وزن، شيئا طفيفا، أي: نزرا حقيرا

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī describes wayl as a valley of Hell’s pus for those who shortchange people in measures and weights, withholding their due full amount; mutaffif comes from something slight or scant.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r1.anchor: والمطفف: المقلل حق صاحب الحق عما له من الوفاء والتمام في كيل أو وزن؛

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r3.claim: When told Medina’s people fulfill measures, ʿAbd Allāh answers that they should, since God warned the fraudulent through the verse about standing before the Lord.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: قال له رجل: يا أبا عبد الرحمن، إن أهل المدينة ليوفون الكيل، قال: وما يمنعهم من أن يوفوا الكيل،

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when the Prophet came to Medina its people were the worst in measure; after the warning was revealed they improved.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: لما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا، فأنزل الله: {ويل للمطففين} [المطففين: 1] فأحسنوا الكيل

TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.claim: ʿIkrima swears that every measurer and weigher is in the Fire: none gives the same measure or weight that they themselves demand.
TAB-FULL:v24p185#2/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: أشهد أن كل كيال ووزان في النار،

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r1.claim: Wayl is nominative as a subject, with li-l-muṭaffifīn as its predicate; nominative is best because their doom is already fixed.

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r2.claim: Outside the Qur'an, waylan in the accusative would mean that God assigned them a doom; the Qur'anic wording cannot be changed against the written text.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r2.anchor:
ولو كان في غير القرآن لجاز
" ويلا " للمطففين، على معنى جعل الله لهم ويلا

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r3.claim: Wayl is an expression used for anyone in punishment and ruin.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r3.anchor: والويل كلمة تقال لكل من هو في عذاب وهلكة

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r4.claim: Muṭaffifūn are people who give short measure or weight.

ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r5.claim: The name comes from taking only a tiny amount in measure or weight, from ṭaff, the edge of something.
ZAJJAJ:v5p297/r5.anchor: وإنما أخذ من طف الشيء وهو جانبه

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.claim: The sura opens by warning those who cheat in measure and weight that they will be resurrected for judgment on the Great Day, then describes the fates of wicked and righteous; context suggests the opening was revealed in Medina.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r1.anchor: تفتتح السورة بوعيد أهل التطفيف في الكيل والوزن وتنذرهم بأنهم مبعوثون للجزاء في يوم عظيم وهو يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:83:1-5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r2.claim: Woe is a threat against those who give short measure or weight; God forbids this and calls it corruption on earth in the story of Shuayb.
TABATABAI:83:1-5/r2.anchor: دعاء على المطففين والتطفيف نقص المكيال والميزان، وقد نهى الله تعالى عنه وسماه إفسادا في الأرض

TABRISI:83:1-3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r1.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم إلا يحيى
TABRISI:83:1-3/r1.claim: Kūfans except ʿĀṣim and Yaḥyā read “ran” with kasra on rāʾ; the other readers use fatḥa.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم إلا يحيى ران بكسر الراء

TABRISI:83:1-3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:83:1-3/r2.claim: Taṭfīf is reducing a measure or weight; a slight amount is called ṭafīf, from the edge of a thing.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r2.anchor: التطفيف نقص المكيال والميزان والطفيف الشيء النزر القليل

TABRISI:83:1-3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:83:1-3/r3.claim: A hadith compares Adam's descendants to a slightly underfilled measure: they are near one another and distinction is by piety.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r3.anchor: كلكم بنو آدم طف الصاع لم تملؤوه فليس لأحد فضل إلا بالتقوى

TABRISI:83:1-3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r13.speaker: عكرمة، ابن عباس
TABRISI:83:1-3/r13.claim: When the Prophet came to Medina, its people were among the worst at measuring; after revelation they improved their measures.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r13.anchor: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا

TABRISI:83:1-3/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:83:1-3/r14.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:83:1-3/r14.claim: Al-Suddī says the verses were revealed about Abū Juhayna, who used one measure when buying and another when selling.
TABRISI:83:1-3/r14.anchor: وبها رجل يقال له أبو جهينة ومعه صاعان يكيل بأحدهما

THALABI:v10p149#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p149#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p149#3/r1.claim: Mutaṭaffifūn are people who shortchange others in measures and weights; ṭafīf means a tiny amount, and a nearly full vessel is called ṭifāf.
THALABI:v10p149#3/r1.anchor: ويل للمطففين يعني الذين ينقصون الناس ويبخسون حقوقهم في الكيل والوزن

THALABI:v10p149#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p149#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p149#3/r2.claim: The idiom كطف الصاع means nearly filling a measure while leaving it short.
THALABI:v10p149#3/r2.anchor: ومنه قيل للقوم الذين يكونون سواء في حسبة أو عدد: هم كطف الصاع

THALABI:v10p150/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p150/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p150/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that people in Medina had been among the worst in measuring when the Prophet arrived; after revelation they measured honestly.
THALABI:v10p150/r1.anchor: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا، فأنزل الله سبحانه ويل للمطففين

THALABI:v10p150/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p150/r2.speaker: القرطبي
THALABI:v10p150/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says Medinan traders used deceptive transactions resembling gambling, mulāmasa, munābadha, and risky sales; the Prophet recited the verse to them in the market.
THALABI:v10p150/r2.anchor: كان بالمدينة تجار يطففون وكانت بياعتهم كشبه القمار والمنابذة والملامسة والمخاطرة

THALABI:v10p150/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p150/r3.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v10p150/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Abu Juhayna used one measure when selling and another when buying, prompting the revelation.
THALABI:v10p150/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة وبها رجل يقال له أبو جهينة ومعه صاعان

THALABI:v10p150/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p150/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p150/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas attributes to the Prophet five social sins and punishments: broken covenants bring enemies, unjust rule brings poverty, sexual immorality brings death, short measure brings crop failure, and withheld zakat brings drought.
THALABI:v10p150/r4.anchor: قال: «ما نقض قوم العهد إلا سلط عليهم عدوهم،

THALABI:v10p150/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p150/r5.speaker: مالك بن دينار
THALABI:v10p150/r5.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says a dying neighbor saw two mountains of fire because he had used separate measures for buying and selling; pounding them together only made them seem larger.
THALABI:v10p150/r5.anchor: قال: يا أبا يحيى كان لي مكيالان، كنت أكيل بأحدهما وأكتال بالآخر

THALABI:v10p151/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p151/r1.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v10p151/r1.claim: Ikrima swore that every measurer or weigher who cheats is destined for Hell, including his own son.
THALABI:v10p151/r1.anchor: سمعت عكرمة يقول: أشهد على كل كيال أو وزان أنه في النار

THALABI:v10p151/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p151/r2.speaker: أعرابي
THALABI:v10p151/r2.claim: An Arab advised against seeking favors from someone whose dignity depends on measuring the top of containers and the teeth of scales.
THALABI:v10p151/r2.anchor: قال لي أعرابي: لا تلتمس الحوائج ممن مروءته في رؤس المكاييل

THALABI:v10p151/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p151/r3.speaker: علي
THALABI:v10p151/r3.claim: Abd Khayr reports that Ali stopped a saffron seller whose measure was heavy, told him first to establish just weight, then allowed him to give extra.
THALABI:v10p151/r3.anchor: عليا مر على رجل وهو يزن الزعفران وقد أرجح، فكفا الميزان، ثم قال: أقم الوزن بالقسط،

THALABI:v10p151/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p151/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v10p151/r4.claim: Ibn Umar warned sellers to fulfill measure and weight, saying cheaters will be detained on Judgment Day until sweat reaches halfway up their ears.
THALABI:v10p151/r4.anchor: وقال نافع كان ابن عمر يمر بالبائع فيقول: اتق الله وأوف الكيل والوزن،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة والمبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mubarrad say a mutaffif is someone who short-measures or short-weighs and does not give the full amount.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r1.anchor: أبو عبيدة (¬2)، والمبرد (¬3): المطفف الذي يبخس في الكيل، والوزن، ولا يوفي، والمطففون: الذين ينقصون المكيال والميزان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r2.claim: Lexicographers connect the word to ṭaff or ṭafāf, the rim-level of a measure that is almost full but not quite; the short-measurer brings it only to that point.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r2.anchor: يقال هذا طف المكيال أو طفافه إذا قارب ملأه ولما يمتلئ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the name refers to short-changing by a very small amount, the slight thing or ṭafīf.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r3.anchor: أبو إسحاق: إنما قيل الذي ينقص المكيال والميزان مطفف، # لأنه لا يكاد يسرق في المكيال، والميزان إلا الشيء اليسير الطفيف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says the verse was revealed when the Prophet came to Medina and its people short-measured for others while demanding full measure for themselves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي: قدم رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- المدينة وهم يسيئون كيلهم ووزنهم لغيرهم، ويستوفون لأنفسهم فنزلت هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra says it was revealed about his uncle Abū Juhayna, who used one measure to take and a different measure to give.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p307#2/r5.anchor: أبو هريرة: نزلت في عمي أبي جهينة (¬3): كان له صاعان يأخذ # بواحد، ويعطي بالأخرى

ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r1.claim: Many authorities, including Suyuti, regard the surah as the last Meccan revelation; some commentators assign the whole surah to Medina.
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r1.anchor: among them Suyuti - regard th is surah as the last Meccan revelation.

ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.claim: Authentic traditions cited by Tabari, Baghawi, and Ibn Kathir place at least the first four verses shortly after the Prophet's arrival in Medina.
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r2.anchor: However, a number of authentic Traditions make it clear that at least the first four verses were

ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r3.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r3.claim: Weighing the evidence, Asad assigns the main body to late Mecca and the opening to early Medina, making the surah a threshold between periods like surah 29.
ASAD-NOTES:83:intro/r3.anchor: the main body of this surah indeed represents the very last Meccan revelation

ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.claim: The condemned demand full measure when receiving from others but give less than their due when measuring or weighing what they owe.
ASAD-NOTES:83:1/r1.anchor: give less than what is due! [1]

ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.claim: The warning extends beyond commerce to every practical and moral social relation, including each person's rights, obligations, and possessions.
ASAD-NOTES:83:1#n1/r1.anchor: does not, of course, refer only to commercial dealings but touches upon every aspect of social relations, both practical and moral

ELMALILI:83:1/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:1/r1.claim: The common Turkish 'vay hâline' fails to convey wail's severity and gives no hint of the report that it is a proper name; 'veyl ona' or 'vâveyla' better reflects its established Turkish usage.
ELMALILI:83:1/r1.anchor: bizim “vay” tâbiri Arabın “veyh” kelimesine mukabil olduğundan veylin şiddetini pek duyurmadığı gibi

ELMALILI:83:1/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:1/r2.claim: Wail has been explained as severe evil, grief and destruction, painful punishment, or a valley in Hell.
ELMALILI:83:1/r2.anchor: hüzn ü helâk, azâb-ı elîm, cehennemde bir vâdi

ELMALILI:83:1/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:1/r3.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Said says Wail is a valley in Hell where a disbeliever falls for forty years before reaching its bottom.
ELMALILI:83:1/r3.anchor: Veyl cehennemde bir vâdidir ki kâfir, ka‘rına varmadan evvel onda kırk yıl sukūt eder

ELMALILI:83:1/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:1/r4.claim: Reports in Ibn Hibban's and Hakim's Sahih collections describe Wail as a valley between two mountains in Hell.
ELMALILI:83:1/r4.anchor: İbn Hibbân’ın ve Hâkim’in Sahîhlerinde: “Cebeleyn beyninde bir vadidir

ELMALILI:83:1/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r5.speaker: Abdullah
ELMALILI:83:1/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Abdullah that Wail is a valley of pus in Hell.
ELMALILI:83:1/r5.anchor: İbn Ebî Hâtim de Abdullah’tan “Cehennemde irinden bir vâdidir” diye rivayet etmiştir

ELMALILI:83:1/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r6.speaker: Asma‘î
ELMALILI:83:1/r6.claim: Asmai says wail means something vile or ugly and can also express regret; those calling it a valley mean that its condemned recipients deserve a place in the fire, not that valley is its lexical meaning.
ELMALILI:83:1/r6.anchor: “‘Veyl’ bir kubuh, yani bir çirkinliktir. Bazen tehassür için de kullanılır

ELMALILI:83:1/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r7.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:83:1/r7.claim: Alusi says applying wail to the recognized sense of Hell appears to be a kind of figurative transfer, though its precise type should be examined.
ELMALILI:83:1/r7.anchor: Ona veyl ıtlak edilmesi cehennemin mâruf olan mânasına ıtlâkı gibi olmak zâhirdir

ELMALILI:83:1/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:1/r8.claim: Elmalılı considers Hell's conventional sense an established religious usage also absorbed into ordinary language, whereas Wail as a particular valley is an unestablished religious metaphor, not common lexicon; 'vay hâline' therefore only partly translates it.
ELMALILI:83:1/r8.anchor: “veyl”in îzah olunan mâna ile cehennemde bir vâdi ismi olması şer‘î bir ıtlak olmakla beraber mütevâtir olmadığı gibi lügaten de müte‘âref olmayan bir mecaz olur

ELMALILI:83:1/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:1/r9.claim: Mutaffifin is the plural of mutaffif: those who take full measure but give less, as the following two verses clarify; Turkish has no exact independent equivalent.
ELMALILI:83:1/r9.anchor: mutaffifler, alırken dolgun, verirken eksik ölçenler demek olduğu önünde sıfat-ı kâşife olan iki âyet ile anlatılmıştır

ELMALILI:83:1/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r10.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:83:1/r10.claim: Razi's first etymology connects tatfif to the edge of a vessel: something reaching its rim without filling it, so the mutaffif gives an incomplete measure.
ELMALILI:83:1/r10.anchor: Bir şeyin taffi, kıyısı ve kenarıdır

ELMALILI:83:1/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:1/r11.claim: The lexicon also uses taff and related forms for a filled measure, its leveled remainder, or its top; on this account tatfif subtracts from the proper measure.
ELMALILI:83:1/r11.anchor: “Taff”, “tafef”, “tafâf”, “tufâf” bir ölçeği veya kabı tam dolduran şeye

ELMALILI:83:1/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r12.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:83:1/r12.claim: Razi's second etymology derives it from a tiny amount: a mutaffif steals a little in measuring or weighing, and the habitual form suits the verse better.
ELMALILI:83:1/r12.anchor: Pek az bir şeye ‘tafîf’ denilir, ölçeği eksik ölçene ‘mutaffif’ denilmesi

ELMALILI:83:1/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:83:1/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:83:1/r13.claim: Elmalılı finds the second derivation more consistent with the verse's description of the mutaffifin.
ELMALILI:83:1/r13.anchor: Bu vecih âyetteki tefsire daha mutâbıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r2.speaker: hadisler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r2.claim: Hadith reports also describe Wayl as the name of a valley in Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r2.anchor: hadislerde cehennemdeki bir vadinin ismi olduğu da bildirilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r3.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r3.claim: Raghib says the valley meaning is figurative: those addressed by wayl will suffer Hell's punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:83:1/r3.anchor: Râgıb el-İsfahânî’ye göre bu kelimenin cehennemdeki bir vadiye isim verilmesi, mecazi anlamda olup

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports, through a chain called sound, that Medinans cheated most in measure when the Prophet arrived; after the verse, they measured properly.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p228/r1.anchor: بسند صحيح عن ابن عباس قال لما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا أبخس الناس كيلا فأنزل الله

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Medinans were especially dishonest in measuring when the Prophet arrived; after the verse was revealed, they measured correctly.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r1.anchor: أن عكرمة حدثه عن ابن عباس قال: لما قدم النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r2.speaker: القرظي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r2.claim: Al-Qurazi says Medinan merchants used deceptive sales resembling games of chance, including munabadha, mulamasa, and mukhatara; the Prophet went to the market and recited this verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r2.anchor: قال القرظي: كان بالمدينة تجار يطففون، وكانت بياعاتهم كشبه القمار

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r3.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse concerned Abu Juhayna, who had two measuring vessels, using one to measure out and another to measure in.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p452/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: قدم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - المدينة وبها رجل يقال له:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.claim: Sūrah al-Muṭaffifīn supplements al-Infiṭār, sharing its theme and elaborating the division of righteous and defiant people at its end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r1.anchor: This sūrah  is a supplement to S ūrah al-Infi ṭār

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.claim: Al-Infiṭār reasons from God’s attributes displayed in the human body, while this sūrah reasons from the moral nature God gave people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r2.anchor: attributes of God that are prominent in man’s physical being

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.claim: Human nature loves justice and good and dislikes injustice and evil; this moral distinction shows that the Creator differentiates the just from the unjust rather than treating them alike.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r3.anchor: by his very nature man likes justice and what is good

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.claim: People commit injustice when other motives overpower their nature, as shown by the dishonest trader who protests when others cheat him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r4.anchor: the very person who is dishonest in weighing to others cries out with anguish if others are dishonest with him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly uses this reasoning for the Day of Judgement; the author points to his discussion of 75:14–15.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p223/r6.anchor: readers can take a look at what I have written under the following verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.claim: Verses 1–6 censure people who demand fair treatment while cheating others; their conduct shows they do not expect to be raised before their Lord for judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p224/r1.anchor: An expression of regret on people who want

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r1.claim: The opening warning is not a neutral statement; it also conveys a curse and censure.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r1.anchor: This sentence is not merely a statement of fact; curse and censure are also concealed in it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.claim: Taṭfīf means giving short measure or weight.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p226/r2.anchor: The word !ْ#ْﺗﻄﻔﻴﻒ refers to measuring and weighing less

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.claim: This nature shows that people distinguish good from evil and expect different treatment; God must therefore judge righteous and wrongdoers, and the deniers resist because they wish to evade that outcome.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r4.anchor: An obvious corollary of this is that the Almighty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.speaker: exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.claim: Exegetes report that dishonest measuring among the Anṣār occasioned revelation of this verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r5.anchor: While explaining this verse, our exegetes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p227/r6.claim: The author challenges that report’s setting: the sūrah is Meccan, and dishonest trade was at least as plausible among the Meccan traders as among the agricultural Anṣār.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.claim: Even if the Anṣār had the practice, it was no more prevalent than among the Meccans, who were traders, while the Anṣār’s profession was agriculture; the verse’s main point is innate recognition of justice, which implies judgement and accountability.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p228/r1.anchor: In fact, there was a much greater chance

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.claim: Taffif is reduction, from something tiny and insignificant; a mutaffif cheats by an inconspicuous small amount in weight or measure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p424/r1.anchor: التطفيف النقصان وأصله من الطفيف وهو النزل الحقير والمطفف الآخذ في وزن أو كيل طفيفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود، الضحاك، مقاتل؛ الحسن، عكرمة، مقاتل؛ ابن عباس، قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r6.claim: The surah is called Meccan by Ibn Masʿud, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil; Medinan by Hasan, Ikrima, and also Muqatil; Ibn Abbas and Qatada say it is Medinan except its last eight verses, which are Meccan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r6.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول ابن مسعود والضحاك ومقاتل، مدنية في قول الحسن وعكرمة ومقاتل أيضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r7.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r7.claim: He says it was revealed in Medina about a man called Abu Juhayna who owned two measures, took with the full one and gave with the short one; it is also said to be the first surah revealed there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: كان بالمدينة رجل يكنى أبا جهينة، له مكيلان، يأخذ بالأوفى ويعطي بالأنقص، فنزلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r8.claim: He says the warning against short measure was revealed in Medina, where the practice was especially corrupt, and the surah corrected people; another account places revelation between Mecca and Medina to reform them before the Prophet arrived.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزل بعضها بمكة، ونزل أمر التطفيف بالمدينة لأنهم كانوا أشد الناس فسادا في هذا المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r9.claim: The prior surah discussed the blessed, the wretched, and the great Day of Judgment; this surah turns to a particularly contemptible sin, cheating in measure for negligible gain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p425/r9.anchor: والمناسبة بين السورتين ظاهرة. لما ذكر تعالى السعداء والأشقياء ويوم الجزاء وعظم شأن يومه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r1.claim: Woe is glossed as severe evil, grief, destruction, painful punishment, or a valley in Hell; a report attributed to Uthman reaches the Prophet but has a questionable chain.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r1.anchor: قيل الويل شدة الشر وقيل الحزن والهلاك وقيل العذاب الأليم وقيل في جهنم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r2.claim: Abu Saʿid reports the Prophet's description of Wail as a valley in Hell into which a disbeliever falls for forty years before reaching its bottom.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ويل واد في جهنم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r3.claim: Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim give a version calling it a valley between two mountains; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Abdullah that it is a Hell valley.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r3.anchor: وفي صحيحي ابن حبان والحاكم بلفظ واد بين جبلين يهوي فيه الكافر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r4.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says the word means shame or ugliness and can also express regret; al-Raghib cautions that the valley interpretation denotes the Hell abode deserved by those God calls wretched, not the dictionary meaning itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r4.anchor: وفي كتاب المفردات للراغب قال الأصمعي ويل قبوح وقد يستعمل للتحسر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r5.claim: Whether it literally names that valley or does so by another semantic relation requires examination; grammatically it can begin a sentence because it functions as a curse, with “to the defrauders” as predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r5.anchor: وأيا ما كان فهو مبتدأ وإن كان نكرة لوقوعه في موقع الدعاء وللمطففين خبره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r6.claim: Defrauding is shortchanging in measure or weight; the root suggests a tiny amount, while the intensive form indicates repeated acts rather than a large amount each time.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r6.anchor: والتطفيف البخس في الكيل والوزن لما أن ما يبخس في كيل أو وزن واحد شيء طفيف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives the word from the edge of a thing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p68/r7.anchor: وعن الزجاج أنه من طف الشيء جانبه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r1.claim: The mutaffifin short measures and weights and withhold people's rights.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r1.anchor: {ويل للمطففين} يعني الذين ينقصون المكيال والميزان ويبخسون حقوق الناس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they are called mutaffifin because the amount skimmed from a measure or weight is usually slight.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: إنما قيل للذي ينقص المكيال والميزان: مطفف لأنه لا يكاد يسرق في المكيال والميزان إلا الشيء اليسير الطفيف.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet arrived in Medina, its people were among the worst in measuring; after the verse came down, they improved their measures.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r4.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about Abu Juhayna, who used one measure when buying and another when selling.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p358#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة وبها رجل يقال له: أبو جهينة ومعه صاعان

BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r1.claim: Taṭfīf is shortchanging in measure or weight because what is withheld is slight or trivial.
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r1.anchor: التطفيف البخس في الكيل والوزن لأن ما يبخس طفيف أي حقير

BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r2.claim: A report says Medina's people were the worst measurers; after this verse came down, they improved their measuring.
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r2.anchor: روي أن أهل المدينة كانوا أخبث الناس كيلا فنزلت فأحسنوه

BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r3.speaker: حديث
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r3.claim: A report warns of enemies for broken covenants, poverty for unjust rule, death with immorality, crop failure and famine for short measure, and withheld rain for unpaid alms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:83:1-2/r3.anchor: ولا طففوا الكيل إلا منعوا النبات وأخذوا بالسنين، ولا منعوا الزكاة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r1.claim: After Sūrat al-Infiṭār stressed judgment and the recording of deeds, the surah warns against fraud in measures and gathers all who share that vice into its threat.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r1.anchor: وكان أعظم ما يدور بين العباد المقادير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r2.claim: Wayl means immense, abiding ruin in every state of worldly and afterlife existence; mutaffifīn are those who reduce measure or weight and withhold people’s rights.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r2.anchor: هلاك ثابت عظيم في كل حال من أحوال الدنيا والآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r3.claim: The author connects petty fraud with bad character and love of the world: habitual cheats come close to a full measure or fair weight but deliberately stop short.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r3.anchor: وهم من يقاربون ملء الكيل وعدل الوزن ولا يملؤون ولا يعدلون

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r4.claim: The word taṭfīf may derive from ṭaff, the edge or projecting rim, and suggest removing what rises above a measure’s top.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r4.anchor: من الطف , وهو ما أشرف من أرض العرب على ريف العراق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar recounts that his horse outpaced others until it nearly reached the Banū Zurayq mosque, illustrating something that rises close to a limit.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r5.anchor: كنت فارسا فسبقت الناس حتى طفت لي الفرس مسجد بني زريق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r6.claim: The author quotes an unattributed saying that people are ‘sons of Adam, the measure’s slight shortfall’ as an example of ṭaff referring to a small amount.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r7.claim: Other proposed roots are taking what is near at hand, as in an almost-full vessel; rationing; or reducing something petty. The author says the word suits fraud because the stolen amount is usually tiny.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#2/r7.anchor: وكأنه اختير هذا اللفظ لأنه لا يكاد يسرق في الميزان والمكيال إلا الشيء اليسير جدا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p356/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the warning to the record of every deed in 82:10 and the exact weighing of deeds in 21:47; fraud may seem small but is a major crime and merits a great warning.

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r1.claim: The chapter is Meccan and has thirty-six verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r1.anchor: مكية وآياتها ست وثلاثون أخرج النحاس

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Surat al-Mutaffifin was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة المطففين بمكة

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr likewise says Surat al-Mutaffifin was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن الزبير مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas also says Surat al-Mutaffifin was the last revelation in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: آخر ما أنزل بمكة سورة المطففين

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r5.claim: 'Woe to those who give short measure' was the first revelation in Medina.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما نزل بالمدينة {ويل للمطففين}

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r6.claim: Medina's people were among the worst in measuring; after this verse was revealed, they measured fairly. Al-Suyuti calls the chain sound.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r6.anchor: بسند صحيح عن ابن عباس قال: لما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس كيلا

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra heard the verse while the Prophet left Sabāʿ ibn ʿArṭafa governing Medina for Khaybar and feared for people using separate measures to give and take.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم استعمل سباع بن عرفطة على المدينة لما خرج إلى خيبر فقرأ

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r8.claim: Ibn Umar wept and applied the verse to an employer or measurer who knowingly cheats, bearing the sin.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه قرأ {ويل للمطففين} فبكى وقال: هو الرجل يستأجر الرجل أو الكيال

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r9.claim: A people who break their covenant are ruled by enemies; those who cheat in measure lose vegetation and suffer drought.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ما نقض قوم العهد إلا سلط الله عليهم عدوهم

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r10.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r10.claim: Prayer is a measure: those who give full measure receive fully, while those who short-measure recall the warning about the mutaffifin.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r10.anchor: عن سلمان قال: إنما الصلاة مكيال فمن أوفى أوفي له ومن طفف فقد سمعتم ما قال الله

DURR-FULL:v8p441/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r11.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r11.claim: Withholding reciprocal recompense is a kind of short measure.
DURR-FULL:v8p441/r11.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه قال: تركك المكافأة تطفيف قال الله: {ويل للمطففين}

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn explains the close of al-Infiṭār: on the Day of Calling, the righteous will settle in bliss and the wicked in the Fire of Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r1.anchor: مقصودها شرح آخر الانفطار بأنه لا بد من دينونة العباد يوم التناد بإسكان الأولياء أهل الرشاد دار النعيم ، والأشقياء أهل الضلال والعناد غار الجحيم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r2.claim: God’s universal beneficence and role as nurturer entail that He will question those He raised and distinguish them fairly; the surah’s name al-Taṭfīf best signals this purpose.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r2.anchor: ودل على ذلك بانه مربيهم والمحسن إليهم بعموم النعمة ، ولا يتخيل عاقل أن أحدا يربي أحدا من غير سؤال عما حمله إياه وكلفه به ولا أنه لا ينصف بعض من يربيهم من بعض ، واسمها التطفيف أدل ما فيها على ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r3.claim: The basmala attributes to God perfect wisdom and power, universal mercy through creation and guidance, and special mercy that grants His party success in good conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p354#s082/r3.anchor: { بسم الله } الذي له الحكمة البالغة والقدرة الكاملة { الرحمن } الذي عم بنعمة الإيجاد والبيان الشاملة

BURHAN:v1p194/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p194/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BURHAN:v1p194/r1.claim: Reports differ on the last revelation in Mecca: Ibn ʿAbbās names al-ʿAnkabūt, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿAṭāʾ name al-Muʾminūn, and Mujāhid names “Woe to those who give short measure.” The author says this ordering is established by reliable transmitters and counts 85 Meccan surahs.
BURHAN:v1p194/r1.anchor: واختلفوا فى آخر ما نزل بمكة فقال ابن عباس العنكبوت
